reason: The board entry orch-strand-cycle (operator decision 2026-10-21) says a strand is live only when its pane sits in the reed session and window it was launched into and its foreground process is the engine (claude), not a shell. Decision record D1 departs three ways: (1) it checks the reed session only, not the window, so a pane moved to another window of the session still reads live and start launches no second orch beside it; (2) it tests that the foreground command is not reed's launch shell rather than that it is claude, keeping reed engine-neutral per PATTERN-shuttle-provider-seam, so another program left running after the engine exited reads live; (3) it skips the foreground check on Windows, so there an exited engine reads live as today. Accept each departure, or hold the run to the entry's rule for it?
